reason: I'll start the bone reconstruction by adding mineral to its collagen framework.
expectation: I expect a mineralized bone framework, probably still needing living cells and blood vessels.

alternatives.reason: The bone-cell lineage also seems necessary, but I'd first build the structural framework.
The lined capsule addresses the other goal, which I can pursue afterward.

effect: The framework now combines collagen and mineral; I still need the living bone lineage and blood supply.
reaction: The contrast between collagen's toughness and mineral's compression resistance is useful.
reason: I'll develop bone-lineage cells to progress toward living bone.
expectation: I expect bone-forming cells or their precursors, though their connection to the mature framework may require another step.

alternatives.reason: The lined capsule is also a goal, but I want to continue the bone branch first.

effect: The lineage produces matrix-making osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes, which can now be combined with the framework or vessels.
reaction: The transition from osteoblasts to embedded osteocytes makes living bone more concrete.
reason: I'll add the bone cells to the mineralised framework to assemble the living bone structure.
expectation: I expect a bone model containing cells within the mineralised matrix, likely still needing a blood supply.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels are also needed, but I want to join the cells to their matrix first.
The capsule remains a separate goal to address afterward.

effect: The bone framework now contains cells linked by fine channels, with its blood supply still unfilled.
reaction: The cutaway makes the cells' place in mature bone clearer.
reason: I'll add blood vessels to complete the bone's supply.
expectation: I expect supplied living arm bones, with vessels shown within the existing bone tissue.

alternatives.reason: The lined capsule is also needed, but I want to finish the bone branch first.

effect: The supplied living bones are complete, and connecting them into a movable joint is now a goal.
reaction: The cutaway's separation of vessels, cells and matrix makes their relationship clearer.
reason: I'll line the fibrous sleeve to progress the remaining capsule goal.
expectation: I expect a joint capsule with a synovial lining that contributes fluid, though it may still need to be joined to the bones.

alternatives.reason: Cartilage should help form the joint surfaces, but I'll prepare the capsule first.

effect: The synovial capsule is complete, with its lining contributing fluid to the joint cavity.
reaction: The distinction between the tough sleeve and fluid-producing lining is clear.
reason: I'll add cartilage to the bones as the only offered combination, progressing toward the movable joint.
expectation: I expect cartilage-covered joint surfaces that can later be joined with the capsule and ligaments.

effect: The bone ends now have cartilage-covered surfaces that can slide against one another.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: I'll join the bones to the capsule; it's the only offered combination and advances the joint goal.
expectation: I expect a fluid-lined elbow joint, possibly still needing ligaments for support.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered ends, with fluid helping them glide; ligaments remain to support the joint.
reaction: The cutaway connects the lining and fluid to the joint's movement clearly.
reason: I'll add the ligaments; it's the only offered combination and should provide restraint.
expectation: I expect a supported, movable elbow joint with ligaments spanning its sides.

effect: The ligaments complete the supported elbow: it bends while resisting sideways movement, and all chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The final arrows clearly distinguish movement from restraint.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building supplied living bone was most worthwhile: the planned cutaway relates mineral-reinforced collagen, embedded cells and blood vessels without conflating them.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding cells to the framework felt somewhat repetitive after the lineage picture had already shown them embedded in mature bone, though the separate assembly clarified their location.

surprise.text: The lineage picture changed my understanding by showing matrix-producing osteoblasts becoming embedded osteocytes with processes through tiny channels.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless. The final joint sequence was predictable and offered only one combination at each step, so it was more guided assembly than a compatibility discovery.

continue.text: I would continue: the connections between tissue structure and joint function were useful, although I would hope for more meaningful choices than the final sequence offered.
